History & Physical (Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
50-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and hypertension presents with a 5- to 6-day history of persistent dry cough and rhinorrhea accompanied by chills, myalgias, and fatigue; clinical impression is an acute viral upper respiratory tract infection with advice for symptomatic care and safety-net follow-up.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Continuous dry cough and runny nose.  
• Onset/duration: Began 5–6 days ago; cough persists day and night and disturbs sleep.  
• Character/progression: Non-productive; no sputum, no hemoptysis.  
• Associated symptoms  
  – Chills/shivering at night (possible fever; temperature not measured)  
  – Generalized myalgias (arms, legs), lethargy/weakness  
  – Transient diarrhea at illness onset; resolved  
  – Mild throat irritation secondary to coughing; no painful swallowing  
  – No ear pain, ear discharge, or blocked ears  
  – No chest pain, no dyspnea on routine exertion; cough episodes briefly cause shortness of breath  
  – No nausea, vomiting; appetite preserved  
  – No urinary symptoms  
  – No skin rash or joint swelling  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None identified; cough worse at night.  
• Review of systems: Otherwise negative as above.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus – controlled with medication; routine primary care follow-up.  
• Hypertension – controlled; routine monitoring.  
Medications:  
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives with partner; partner well and asymptomatic.  
• Occupation: IT developer; sedentary job. Missed 1 workday due to illness.  
• Tobacco: Former smoker; quit 6 months ago.  
• Alcohol: Wine 2–3 glasses on ~3 evenings per week (≈6–9 glasses/week). Counseled to reduce intake.  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.  
• Exercise: Occasional Pilates (currently limited by myalgias).

Family History:
• Father: Type 2 diabetes.  
• Otherwise non-contributory.

Physical Examination:
(No vitals or exam findings documented during tele-consult.)

Investigations:
None performed or reported.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection / influenza-like illness  
• Assessment: Symptom cluster (dry cough, rhinorrhea, chills, myalgias, transient diarrhea) and 5-day course most consistent with self-limiting viral illness. Bacterial pneumonia, ACE-inhibitor cough, and other causes considered less likely at this stage.  
• Plan:  
  – Supportive care: rest, adequate hydration, regular acetaminophen (paracetamol) for discomfort/fever.  
  – Workplace advice: Take 1–2 additional days off to rest and limit spread.  
  – Safety-net: Return or seek care sooner if cough worsens, breathing becomes difficult, sustained fever develops, or no improvement within 2–3 days. Consider chest exam and possible antibiotics if bacterial superinfection suspected.

Issue 2 – Chronic disease management (Type 2 diabetes, Hypertension)  
• Assessment: Conditions currently “under control” per patient; no acute complications reported.  
• Plan:  
  – Continue Metformin and Lisinopril as prescribed.  
  – Reinforce lifestyle measures: maintain smoking cessation, gradual reduction of alcohol (target ≤2 glasses/week initially, aiming for further reduction), balanced diet, regular exercise once recovered.  
  – Routine follow-up with primary care for blood pressure and HbA1c monitoring.

Issue 3 – General wellbeing / convalescence  
• Plan: Encourage gradual return to normal activity as tolerated; resume Pilates when myalgias resolve.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection / influenza-like illness – High likelihood; classic symptom constellation with short duration.
2. Acute viral bronchitis / post-viral cough – Moderate likelihood; cough predominant but duration still short (<1 week).
3. Community-acquired atypical pneumonia – Low to moderate likelihood; consider if fever or respiratory status worsens; diabetes is a risk factor.  

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: No vital signs, lung or general physical examination documented; medication doses/frequencies not recorded; immunization status (influenza/COVID) not addressed; blood glucose control parameters not reviewed.  
• Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional pauses but clinically sufficient.
